topic.title: How deep Hampstead goes: the deepest lift shaft and platforms on the London Underground, the never-opened North End station and the long emergency stair

title: How Deep Does London's Deepest Station Go?
description:
How deep does London's deepest station go?
Under a hill in north London sit the deepest lift shaft and platforms on the Underground, a station further up the line that never opened, and a very long emergency stair.
Sources: Wikipedia, TfL Art on the Underground (2025).
Depths from published sources. Cutaway illustrations, not to scale.
cta: Lift or stairs: which would you take? Comment

lines.text: London's deepest Tube station has no escalators at all. What's under Hampstead?
55 m: the lifts drop straight down a shaft.
58.5 m: the Northern line platforms, the deepest in London.
Further up the line, deeper still, at 221 ft: North End, a station that never opened.
And the emergency stair back up has 320 steps.
All the way up to Hampstead.

Re-review after the northend line changed to 'Further up the line, deeper still, at 221 ft: North End, a station that never opened.' 'Deeper still' is correct: 221 ft (67 m) is below Hampstead's 58.5 m (192 ft) platforms, and Wikipedia (North End tube station) says North End would have been the deepest below ground on the whole Underground. All earlier confirmations stand: 55 m lift shaft and 58.5 m platforms (Wikipedia Hampstead), 320 steps (TfL Labyrinth), no escalators (ianvisits), disclaimer present in the description.

Re-review 3: four or more places (Hampstead's tiled front, lift shaft, Northern platform with a train standing at 10s, North End's own dark hall with plans, crates and its 221 FT sign at 15s, stair pull-back with the STEPS 320 counter); the meter matches each sign (55 m, 58.5 m, 67 m); the thumbnail 'How deep is Hampstead?' differs from v-53's; 23 s, peak -1 dB, mean -16.2 dB, no layout or craft problems. Accepted: at 20s the caption crosses the tiny NORTHERN sign in the stack, which is only scenery there.

Facts confirmed on source pages: 55 m deepest lift shaft and 58.5 m platforms, deepest on the Underground (Wikipedia Hampstead tube station); North End 221 ft/67 m, never opened, between Hampstead and Golders Green (Wikipedia North End); 320 steps, most of any Tube station (art.tfl.gov.uk Labyrinth Hampstead). The no-escalators hook is confirmed by ianvisits (4 lifts, 0 escalators) and Diamond Geezer (sign on the spiral stair: over 320 steps). Verify list met: 221 ft is told as North End, not the platforms, and 320 is credited to TfL (one older source gives 310). The description ends with the channel disclaimer. Notes: TfL gives 320 as the station's total steps, and the 'emergency stair' framing rests on secondary sources. North End was only partly built, so 'a station that never opened' is accurate.

[scene] Thumbnail and 0.0s/22.3s: the same picture as v-20261121-53's (identical three-arched-window facade, two taxis at the doors, shaft at left, same framing), only the colour and words changed; Hampstead's station preset draws Grand Central's front painted red. The thumbnail's HAMPSTEAD sign is blurred out, the words read 'HOW DEEP HAMPSTEAD?' (ungrammatical), and the 'LONDON' label at 0.0s and in the thumbnail is cut off by the right-hand shaft.

[script] 20.0s (steps beat, Hampstead's emergency stair): the depth meter reads '67 m / 221 ft', North End's depth, and the pull-back stacks North End directly under Hampstead's lifts, so the stair looks like it climbs from North End; the meter should sit at Hampstead's platform depth (58.5 m) and North End should not read as part of Hampstead's stack.

[script] 15.0s vs 10.0s: the North End beat shows the same picture as the Northern platform beat (an empty horizontal tunnel band with orange/blue stripes, a sign, beige soil); no 'dark empty station hall', lamp or UNOPENED stamp is visible, and nothing happens in it. Also North End's sign (221 FT) is already on screen at 10.0s, before the turn is spoken, and the voice switches from metres (55 m, 58.5 m) to feet (221 ft), so a listener can't hear that North End is deeper; say it in metres like the others.

[scene] Weaker than v-20261121-53: the 5.0s, 10.0s and 15.0s stills are mostly flat beige soil with empty tunnels (no train, no riders; the lift car is a tiny green dot at 5.0s), where 53's stills all show trains and riders in motion. Also 10.0s: the meter's '59 m' disagrees with the sign's '58.5 M' next to it (rounding).
